--- title: "stateMINT internals" --- ## Architecture stateMINT is built on Mamba2, a state-space sequence model whose mechanism is a linear recurrence, carrying a hidden state of width `d_state` = 128 from one timestep to the next, updating it with the current input and reading the output from it. It is causal. The prediction at step $t$ depends only on the inputs up to $t$. A linear projection lifts the 16 input features to `d_model` = 256, two Mamba2 blocks run over the sequence, dropout is applied, and a linear head reads one output per timestep. ::: {#d13e2014 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from stateMINT.model import Mamba2Regressor prevalence = Mamba2Regressor.from_pretrained( "dide-ic/stateMINT", predictor="prevalence", revision="v1.2.2", ) cases = Mamba2Regressor.from_pretrained( "dide-ic/stateMINT", predictor="cases", revision="v1.2.2", ) prevalence.model_config ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'model_type': 'Mamba2Regressor', 'predictor': 'prevalence', 'input_size': 16, 'd_model': 256, 'n_layers': 2, 'd_state': 128, 'd_conv': 4, 'expand': 2, 'head_dim': 64, 'chunk_size': 256, 'output_dim': 1, 'dropout': 0.24} ``` ::: ::: The two predictors are separately trained checkpoints of the same architecture, sharing no weights, no scaler, not even a dropout rate. ::: {#ebca5343 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} print("cases dropout :", cases.model_config["dropout"]) print("prevalence dropout:", prevalence.model_config["dropout"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` cases dropout : 0.29 prevalence dropout: 0.24 ``` ::: ::: ## The input tensor `prepare_inputs` turns a list of covariate dicts into a `(B, 157, 16)` array. | Columns | Group | What they are | |---|---|---| | 0–1 | Cyclical time | The sine and cosine of the day of year, giving the model a smooth, wrapped calendar rather than a sawtooth | | 2–13 | Static covariates | The twelve covariates, standardised, broadcast across every timestep | | 14–15 | Intervention | A post-campaign flag, and years since the campaign | ::: {#8aaad300 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np config = prevalence.preprocessing_config covariates = dict( eir=31.96, dn0_use=0.311, dn0_future=0.457, Q0=0.85, phi_bednets=0.80, seasonal=0.0, routine=0.0, itn_use=0.70, irs_use=0.0, itn_future=0.70, irs_future=0.0, lsm=0.0, ) X = prevalence.prepare_inputs([covariates]) print("shape:", X.shape, X.dtype) print("static covariates:", config["static_covars"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` shape: (1, 157, 16) float32 static covariates: ['eir', 'dn0_use', 'dn0_future', 'Q0', 'phi_bednets', 'seasonal', 'routine', 'itn_use', 'irs_use', 'itn_future', 'irs_future', 'lsm'] ``` ::: ::: The static block is the same twelve numbers repeated 157 times, apart from the five after-intervention covariates, which are zeroed before day 3285 (please see [Pipeline architecture](architecture.qmd)). ::: {#4d24f3e9 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} abs_t = np.arange( config["model_start_day"], config["model_start_day"] + config["window_size"] * config["n_steps"], config["window_size"], ) years = (abs_t - config["intervention_day"]) / 365 fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 3.4)) axes[0].plot(years, X[0, :, 0], label="sin(day of year)") axes[0].plot(years, X[0, :, 1], label="cos(day of year)") axes[0].set_ylabel("cyclical time") axes[1].plot(years, X[0, :, 14], label="post-campaign flag") axes[1].plot(years, X[0, :, 15], label="years since campaign") axes[1].set_ylabel("intervention features") for ax in axes: ax.axvline(0, color="#8b93a3", ls="--", lw=1, alpha=0.7) ax.set_xlabel("years from campaign") ax.legend() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![The four time-varying features of the input tensor. The dashed rule marks the campaign at day 3285.](statemint-internals_files/figure-html/cell-6-output-1.png){fig-alt='Two panels. Left: sine and cosine of the day of year, oscillating over six years. Right: a post-campaign step from 0 to 1 at year 0, and a years-since-campaign ramp rising linearly from 0 to about 3.'} ::: ::: The blue and orange curves in the left panel wind through six cycles without a break. The pair gives `seasonal` its effect, a phase for the seasonal amplitude to attach to. In the right panel the blue flag steps to 1 at the campaign, while the orange ramp climbs linearly from there, telling the model both that the campaign has happened and how long ago. Waning is learned against time since deployment. ## Standardisation The twelve static covariates are standardised before the input projection, because they sit on very different scales. The scaler is not a pickle. It is two lists of plain JSON in `preprocessing_config`, `scaler_mean` and `scaler_scale`, from which a `StandardScaler` is rebuilt at load. Each covariate is transformed as $(x - \mu) / s$. ::: {#b16aa711 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd pd.DataFrame({ "covariate": config["static_covars"], "scaler_mean": config["scaler_mean"], "scaler_scale": config["scaler_scale"], }) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
covariate scaler_mean scaler_scale
0 eir 58.740086 104.591171
1 dn0_use 0.316041 0.160086
2 dn0_future 0.317523 0.159465
3 Q0 0.797899 0.117432
4 phi_bednets 0.663672 0.160268
5 seasonal 0.482501 0.499694
6 routine 0.487877 0.499853
7 itn_use 0.251948 0.324602
8 irs_use 0.156345 0.262696
9 itn_future 0.253129 0.323122
10 irs_future 0.175586 0.288651
11 lsm 0.245483 0.321897
``` ::: ::: The scaler's means and standard deviations are those of the simulations the emulator was fitted to, so an EIR of 400 sits 3.3 standard deviations out from the training mean. The model will return a value there, but it is not one to rely on. Masking happens in raw units and standardisation afterwards, so a pre-campaign `itn_future` appears in the tensor as $(0 - \mu) / s$, not as 0. ## Target transforms Prevalence is a proportion and is learned in **logit** space, while cases are counts with a long right tail and are learned in **log1p** space. `predict` inverts the transform for you, a sigmoid for prevalence and `expm1` for cases. Pass `transformed=True` for the model's own space. ::: {#bab787f0 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} z = prevalence.predict([covariates], transformed=True) y = prevalence.predict([covariates]) print("logit space:", z.min().round(3), "to", z.max().round(3)) print("prevalence :", y.min().round(3), "to", y.max().round(3)) print("sigmoid(z) == y:", np.allclose(1 / (1 + np.exp(-z)), y, atol=1e-6)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` logit space: -1.034 to 0.059 prevalence : 0.262 to 0.515 sigmoid(z) == y: True ``` ::: ::: ::: {#575a9e83 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} z_cases = cases.predict([covariates], transformed=True) y_cases = cases.predict([covariates]) print("expm1(z) == y :", np.allclose(np.expm1(z_cases), y_cases, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-4)) print("smallest log1p :", float(z_cases.min())) print("smallest cases :", float(y_cases.min())) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` expm1(z) == y : True smallest log1p : 0.3220270276069641 smallest cases : 0.3799220025539398 ``` ::: ::: Prevalence is bounded by construction, because a sigmoid cannot leave [0, 1], while `expm1` is not bounded below, and when the head's log1p output falls under zero, as it can after an effective campaign in a low-burden setting, `predict` returns a case count slightly below zero. `run_scenarios` floors the case series with `np.maximum(..., 0.0)`. A bare `predict` does not. ## The weights repository Weights live on Hugging Face at `dide-ic/stateMINT`, one folder per predictor. ```{.text .diagram} dide-ic/stateMINT ├── prevalence/ │ ├── checkpoint/ # Orbax │ ├── model_config.json │ └── preprocessing_config.json └── cases/ ├── checkpoint/ ├── model_config.json └── preprocessing_config.json ``` `from_pretrained` downloads only the subfolder for the predictor you asked for, restores the Orbax checkpoint into a `Mamba2Regressor` built from `model_config.json`, rebuilds the scaler from `preprocessing_config.json`, and hands back a `ModelArtifact` holding all four. ## See also [Covariates and the time grid](../05-statemint/covariates.qmd) sets out the covariates as a user supplies them. Please see [Performance and caching](../05-statemint/performance.qmd) for what the download and the first `predict` call cost.
